input: Prepare me for a meeting with Monday.com (monday.com)

challenges.evidence: "After its stock plunged 73% over the past year amid investor concerns that artificial intelligence could undermine its business model... monday.com is going on the offensive. Seeking to shake off its status as one of the symbols of the so-called 'SaaS apocalypse'..."
challenges.challenge: AI-disruption fears ("SaaS apocalypse") hammering the stock

challenges.evidence: Mann and Zinman called it the company's "most painful decision" since founding: "Without a fundamental change in how we operate, we will not be able to compete and win that market"; the company says margins were not the purpose and savings will be reinvested in AI and growth.
challenges.challenge: Painful restructuring: ~20% of global workforce cut (~620 jobs)

challenges.evidence: "good results are no longer enough"; the selloff took market value to roughly $3.6 billion; "For investors already skeptical of monday.com's ability to navigate the AI disruption, conservative guidance can look less like prudence and more like a warning."
challenges.challenge: Investor skepticism despite beats — shares fell up to 12% after Q2 2026 because full-year guidance was left unchanged

challenges.evidence: "Investors are concerned that Google's shift to AI-generated search summaries has hurt click-through rates on ads. Monday admits that this has impacted small-business leads, but said that large enterprise demand remains strong."
challenges.challenge: AI is disrupting monday.com's own go-to-market: Google AI-generated search results are hurting paid-search lead generation from SMBs

key_people.name: Eran Zinman
key_people.title: Co-Founder & Co-CEO
key_people.recent: Co-signed the layoff letter calling the restructure the "most painful decision" since founding; told investors Q3 2025 showed acceleration across $50K/$100K/$500K customer cohorts and that the company is "firmly on track toward our Investor Day revenue target of $1.8 billion for FY 2027."

key_people.name: Casey George
key_people.title: Chief Revenue Officer
key_people.recent: Leading the upmarket sales push; highlighted that only 6% of customers consume more than one product, calling the multi-product cross-sell opportunity "significant," while flagging longer, back-weighted enterprise sales cycles.

key_people.name: Daniel Lereya
key_people.title: Chief Product & Technology Officer
key_people.recent: Owns the product portfolio being rebuilt around AI agents (monday Vibe, Agent Factory, AI credits, monday MCP, Microsoft Copilot integration) as the company shifts from managing work to doing the work.

key_people.name: Roy Mann
key_people.title: Co-Founder & Co-CEO
key_people.recent: Framed the company's re-vision as "the most significant change in monday's history" — from work management to an AI-agent platform that performs work — and launched monday Ventures; steered the 620-person restructuring and won ~99% shareholder approval for a ~$14M annual pay package.

key_people.name: Eliran Glazer
key_people.title: Chief Financial Officer
key_people.recent: Reported record non-GAAP operating profit and steered the guidance policy investors keep punishing (FY2026 guidance held at ~$1.47B in Aug 2026); pushing RPO as the better forward-revenue metric and championing "efficient, profitable growth."

priorities.evidence: On the Q3 2025 call: monday Vibe users created 60,000+ apps since July, prompting tiered AI-usage pricing; Agent Factory launched for building AI agents with consumption-based pricing; a new AI credit system was rolling out in Q4. New products already exceeded 10% of total ARR ahead of schedule.
priorities.priority: Monetizing new AI products — monday Vibe, Agent Factory, and a new AI credit/pricing system

priorities.evidence: Co-founders Roy Mann and Eran Zinman told employees: "Over the past nine months, we have shifted our core vision moving from managing work to doing the work for our customers, with people and AI agents working together in one workspace" — and restructured the company around smaller autonomous teams for the AI era.
priorities.priority: Pivot from a work-management platform to an AI-agent platform where people and AI agents do the work together

priorities.evidence: monday.com launched monday Ventures with up to $200M (initial $50M already deploying, led by Aviel Ichai, ex-NEXT47), backing AI-agent, enterprise-AI and workflow-automation startups (Blocks.diy seed, Guidde $50M Series B, NanoCo $12M seed). Roy Mann: "we rebuilt our platform around a model in which people and AI agents work together. The launch of monday Ventures is a direct extension of that vision."
priorities.priority: monday Ventures: a venture arm allocating up to $200 million to AI startups

priorities.evidence: Q2 2026: customers with >$500K ARR rose 68% YoY to 114 and >$100K ARR customers rose 37% to 2,019, now 30% of total ARR; management: large customers "want to consolidate suppliers and are also looking for large platforms that have already moved to AI, which gives us a tailwind."
priorities.priority: Upmarket / enterprise expansion and multi-product consolidation

priorities.evidence: "Monday.com expects growth to accelerate in the second half of 2026 as new AI products gain traction... betting that its transformation from software that helps employees manage work into software that can actually perform work will eventually create a new growth engine"; FY2026 revenue guidance held at $1.466–1.474 billion.
priorities.priority: Accelerating growth in H2 2026 by turning the AI transformation into a new growth engine

what_they_do.value: monday.com describes itself as "the AI work platform that not only helps manage and orchestrate work, but also does the work for you" — around 250,000 customers use it to bring people, workflows, and AI agents together on one flexible platform, spanning work management, CRM, service and dev products on a shared AI layer.

recent_changes.summary: Q2 2026 beat expectations with rapid AI-product growth and continued large-customer expansion (>$500K ARR customers +68% YoY to 114), but shares fell as much as 12% after full-year 2026 revenue guidance was held at $1.466–1.474 billion; market value ~$3.6 billion.
recent_changes.headline: Monday is doing almost everything right. Wall Street still isn't convinced

recent_changes.summary: Shareholders approved (~99% in favor) a near-doubling of co-CEO compensation to ~$14 million a year each for Roy Mann and Eran Zinman, up from ~$7.2 million since 2021 — approved amid slowing growth, a falling share price and the 620-person workforce reduction.
recent_changes.headline: Monday shareholders back $14 million CEO pay packages despite layoffs

recent_changes.summary: monday.com cut ~20% of its global workforce (~620 roles) to rebuild the organization for the AI-agent era — fewer management layers, smaller autonomous teams, and a changed selling model — with savings earmarked for reinvestment in AI and growth rather than margins.
recent_changes.headline: Monday.com cuts 20% of workforce as it restructures for the AI era

talking_points: With only ~6% of customers consuming more than one product and large enterprises consolidating suppliers onto AI-ready platforms, ask how their cross-sell/enterprise expansion is progressing and where they need help landing multi-product, upmarket deals.

Monday.com rebuilt itself around "people and AI agents working together" — asking how the buyer's teams are preparing for AI agents executing work inside their work-management platform, not just tracking it.

Investors punish even strong quarters when guidance is flat — ask what internal evidence (Vibe usage, Agent Factory adoption, RPO acceleration) they need to see before growth re-accelerates in H2 2026, and how a vendor could help prove that AI momentum to the market.
